title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Identifying the Certificate Behind Incoming Proceeds
content:
When the holder of a Savings & Money Market Accounts product wants the proceeds of a certificate of deposit moved back out, the certificate in question has to be pinned down from the records, not from the owner's description. This page defines which certificate that is.

## Rule

**Where to look.** Among the deposits on this savings or money market account that posted as internal transfers, take the one with the latest posting date. The account on the other side of that deposit is the candidate.

**The candidate must be the right kind of account.** It counts as the paying certificate only if the Certificates of Deposit records show it to be a certificate belonging to the same customer and naming this very savings or money market account as its payout account.

**When no certificate is identified.** If the latest internal-transfer deposit came from anything else, such as a checking account or a certificate paying elsewhere, no certificate money is identified and nothing moves under this policy.

**When the latest date is shared.** Should that latest date carry internal-transfer deposits from more than one sending account, no order among them can be read from the ledger, and again nothing moves under this policy. Several deposits on that date from one and the same account raise no such doubt.

## Input, judgement, output

| What the records show | Judgement | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Latest internal-transfer deposit came from a certificate of this customer whose payout account is this account | candidate confirmed | that certificate is the paying certificate |
| Latest internal-transfer deposit came from the customer's checking account | not a certificate | no certificate money; nothing moved |
| Latest internal-transfer deposit came from a certificate whose payout account is a different account | payout link missing | no certificate money; nothing moved |
| On the latest date, internal-transfer deposits arrived from a certificate and from a checking account | latest source unclear | nothing moved |

## Hypothetical case

A money market account received an internal transfer from a certificate on 3 June and another internal transfer from the owner's checking account on 9 June. The latest internal-transfer deposit is the 9 June one, from checking, so no paying certificate is identified, even though a certificate paid in earlier.
